record.paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
record.original_question: Assume L1[0,1] Gδ-embeds into a Banach space X and Y is a subspace of X. Must L1[0,1] Gδ-embed into Y or into the quotient X/Y? Likewise, if L1[0,1] semi-embeds into X and Y is a subspace of X, must L1[0,1] semi-embed into Y or into X/Y?

evidence.quote: Problem 15. A) Suppose that L1 Gδ -embeds into a Banach space X and let Y be a subspace of X . Does L1 Gδ -embed either into Y or into X/Y ? B) Suppose that L1 semi-embeds into a Banach space X and let Y be a subspace of X . Does L1 semi-embed either into Y or into X/Y ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L_1 := L_1[0,1]$ denote the Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue-integrable real-valued functions on $[0,1]$. Recall the following weak notions of embedding between Banach spaces $E$ and $F$:

(i) A bounded linear operator $T: E \to F$ is called a $G_\delta$-embedding if $T$ is injective and $T(B_E)$ is a $G_\delta$-subset of $F$, where $B_E$ is the closed unit ball of $E$. We say $E$ $G_\delta$-embeds into $F$ if such a $T$ exists.

(ii) A bounded linear operator $T: E \to F$ is called a semi-embedding if $T$ is injective and $T(B_E)$ is closed in $F$. We say $E$ semi-embeds into $F$ if such a $T$ exists.

Let $X$ be a Banach space and $Y$ a closed subspace of $X$. Determine whether the following implications hold:

(A) If $L_1$ $G_\delta$-embeds into $X$, must $L_1$ $G_\delta$-embed into $Y$ or into the quotient $X/Y$?

(B) If $L_1$ semi-embeds into $X$, must $L_1$ semi-embed into $Y$ or into the quotient $X/Y$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a list of open problems on $L_1$. A targeted web search did not surface any subsequent paper announcing a solution to either part (A) or (B). The closest related results concern semi-embeddings of $L_1$ implying containment of $\ell_1$, and structural results on quotients of $L_1$ by reflexive subspaces, but none directly resolve the three-space-type question as stated. Status appears to remain open, though this could not be definitively confirmed.

status_evidence.title: Applications of the theory of semi-embeddings to Banach space theory
status_evidence.snippet: If L1 semi-embeds in Y, then Y fails the Schur property and contains a subspace isomorphic to l1.
status_evidence.claim: Background result on semi-embeddings of L1, but does not address the three-space question.

status_evidence.title: Quotients of L1 by reflexive subspaces
status_evidence.snippet: There is no infinite-dimensional reflexive subspace Z of L1[0,1] such that the quotient L1/Z is isomorphic to a subspace of L1.
status_evidence.claim: Related structural result on quotients of L1, not a resolution of the problem.
